title.zh: 卷一百零三 列傳第二十八 蘇世長子:良嗣 從孫:弁 韋雲起孫:方質 孫伏伽 張玄素
title.en: Volume 103 Biographies 28: Su Shizhang and Son: Liang Si, Newphew: Bian, Wei Yunqi and Grandson: Fang Zhi, Sun Fujia, Zhang Xuansu
title.raw: 卷一百零三 列傳第二十八 蘇世長子:良嗣 從孫:弁 韋雲起孫:方質 孫伏伽 張玄素 Volume 103 Biographies 28: Su Shizhang and Son: Liang Si, Newphew: Bian, Wei Yunqi and Grandson: Fang Zhi, Sun Fujia, Zhang Xuansu

sentences.zh: 蘇世長子:良嗣 從孫:弁 韋雲起孫:方質 孫伏伽 張玄素

translations.literal: Su Shichang, son: Liangsi, grandnephew: Bian, Wei Yunqi's grandson: Fang Zhi, Sun Fuga, Zhang Xuansu
translations.idiomatic: Su Shichang; his son Liangsi; his grandnephew Bian; Wei Yunqi's grandson Fang Zhi; Sun Fuga; and Zhang Xuansu

sentences.zh: 蘇世長

translations.literal: Su Shichang
translations.idiomatic: Su Shichang

sentences.zh: 蘇世長，京兆武功人。

translations.literal: Su Shichang was a man of Wugong in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shichang was a native of Wugong in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 祖彤，仕後魏通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong served the Later Wei as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong had served the Northern Wei as Director of the Palace Library and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父振，周宕州刺史，建威縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Danzhou under Zhou and Marquis of Jianwei County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been governor of Danzhou under the Zhou and held the title Marquis of Jianwei County.

sentences.zh: 世長十餘歲，上書周武帝，帝異其幼，問讀何書，對「治《孝經》、《論語》」。

translations.literal: When Shichang was a little over ten, he submitted a memorial to Emperor Wu of Zhou. The Emperor was struck by his youth and asked what books he studied. He replied, "I study the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."
translations.idiomatic: When Shichang was barely into his teens, he sent a memorial to Emperor Wu of Zhou. The emperor marveled at his youth and asked what texts he had been reading. Shichang answered that he was studying the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何言可道？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "What saying can you offer?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What teaching can you put into words?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「為國者不敢侮於鰥寡。

translations.literal: He answered, "One who governs a state does not dare to slight widowers and widows.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Whoever rules a state must not look down on widowers and widows.

sentences.zh: 為政以德。」

translations.literal: To govern is to employ virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Governing means ruling through virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 使卒學虎門館。

translations.literal: He had him finish his studies at the Humen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent him to complete his studies at the Humen Academy.

sentences.zh: 父死王事，有詔襲爵，世長號踴不自勝，帝奭然改容。

translations.literal: When his father died in the ruler's service, an edict ordered him to inherit the title. Shichang wailed and stamped his feet beyond bearing; the Emperor looked startled and his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died in the sovereign's service, an edict directed Shichang to succeed to the title. He broke into loud mourning and could not control his grief; the emperor's face fell in sudden solemnity.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為長安令，數條上便宜。

translations.literal: Entering the Sui, he became Magistrate of Chang'an and repeatedly submitted proposals on what would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as magistrate of Chang'an and repeatedly memorialized the throne with practical policy suggestions.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為都水少監，督漕上江。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he was Vice Director of the Directorate of Waterways, supervising grain transport up the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era he was appointed vice director of waterways and oversaw grain transport on the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 會煬帝被弑，發喪，慟聞行路。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was assassinated, he proclaimed mourning; his grief was heard along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was murdered, he publicly mourned him, and his lament was so piercing that travelers on the road could hear it.

sentences.zh: 更為王世充太子太保、行台右僕射，與世充兄子弘烈及其將豆盧行褒戍襄陽，高祖與之舊，數遣使者諭降，輒殺之。

translations.literal: He then became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat for Wang Shichong, and with Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Xingbao guarded Xiangyang. Gaozu had known him of old and repeatedly sent envoys to urge surrender, but he always killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Wang Shichong as grand mentor of the heir apparent and right vice director of the mobile secretariat, and with Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Xingbao he held Xiangyang. Gaozu, who had known him in earlier days, sent envoys again and again to win him over, but Shichang had every one of them put to death.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，始與弘烈歸，帝誅褒而誚世長，頓首謝曰：「古帝王受命，以此逐鹿，一人得禽，萬夫斂手。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, he and Honglie at last submitted. The Emperor executed Xingbao and reproached Shichang. Bowing his head, he apologized and said, "In antiquity when emperors received the Mandate, they used this means to contend for the realm; when one man took the quarry, ten thousand men folded their hands.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell, he and Honglie finally came over. The emperor executed Xingbao and rebuked Shichang. Shichang kowtowed and said, "In ancient times, when a ruler received Heaven's mandate, he joined the hunt for empire; once one man seized the prize, all the rest laid down their bows.

sentences.zh: 豈有獲鹿後忿同獵者，問爭肉罪邪？

translations.literal: How could there be, after the deer was taken, resentment toward fellow hunters and inquiry into the crime of quarreling over the meat?
translations.idiomatic: Surely no victor, having taken the stag, would then turn on his fellow hunters and charge them with fighting over the carcass?

sentences.zh: 今陛下應天順民，安可忘管仲、雍齒事？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people—how can you forget the affairs of Guan Zhong and Yong Chi?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now answers Heaven and wins the people—will you forget how Guan Zhong and Yong Chi were treated?

sentences.zh: 且武功舊人，亂離以來，死亡略盡，唯臣得見太平。

translations.literal: Moreover, of the old men of Wugong, since the turmoil and separation, death has nearly taken them all; only I have lived to see peace.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, of the old companions from Wugong, nearly all have perished in the years of chaos; I alone have lived to see peace restored.

sentences.zh: 若殺之，是絕其類。」

translations.literal: If you kill me, you will cut off that line.
translations.idiomatic: If you execute me now, you will wipe out the last of our kind.

sentences.zh: 帝笑釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 授玉山屯監。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Yushan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the post of supervisor of the Yushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 引見玄武門，與語平生，調之曰：「卿自謂佞邪，直邪？」

translations.literal: He was summoned to an audience at the Xuanwu Gate and spoke of his whole life. The Emperor teased him, saying, "Do you call yourself a flatterer or a straight speaker?
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience at the Xuanwu Gate, he talked over his whole career with the emperor, who jested, "Do you take yourself for a sycophant or an honest man?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「愚且直。」

translations.literal: He answered, "I am foolish and yet straight."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Foolish, perhaps—but honest."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若直者，何為背賊歸我？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If you are straight, why did you turn from the rebel and come to me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you are so honest, why did you desert the rebel and come to me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「洛陽平，天下為一，臣智窮力屈，乃歸陛下。

translations.literal: He answered, "When Luoyang was pacified, the realm became one. My wits were exhausted and my strength spent, and only then did I submit to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Once Luoyang fell and the realm was united, my wits were spent and my strength broken—only then did I yield to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 使世充不死，臣據漢南，尚為勍敵。」

translations.literal: Had Shichong not died, with me holding the south of the Han, I would still have been a formidable foe."
translations.idiomatic: Had Shichong lived on and I still held the lands south of the Han, I would have remained a formidable enemy."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，嘲曰：「何名長而意之短，口正而心之邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed loudly and mocked him, saying, "Why is your name Long yet your intent short, your mouth straight yet your heart crooked?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter and mocked him: "Your name means 'long,' yet your designs are short; your mouth is straight, but is your heart?"

sentences.zh: 世長曰：「名長意短，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: Shichang said, "Name long, intent short—truly as Your Sagely Majesty says.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang said, "That my name is Long while my aims are short—Your Majesty is quite right.

sentences.zh: 口正心邪，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Mouth straight, heart crooked—I dare not accept that edict.
translations.idiomatic: But that my mouth is honest while my heart is crooked—I cannot accept that charge.

sentences.zh: 昔竇融以河西降漢，十世侯之；

translations.literal: Formerly Dou Rong surrendered Hexi to the Han and was enfeoffed for ten generations;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Dou Rong surrendered the Hexi region to the Han and his house was enfeoffed for ten generations;

sentences.zh: 臣舉山南以歸，唯蒙屯監。」

translations.literal: I raised the lands south of the mountains and submitted—yet I receive only a garrison supervisor."
translations.idiomatic: I brought in the whole region south of the mountains, yet all I receive is a garrison supervisor's post."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and appointed him Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and appointed him remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 從獵涇陽，大獲。

translations.literal: Accompanying a hunt at Jingyang, they took a great catch.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Jingyang the party took an abundant kill.

sentences.zh: 帝入旌門，詫左右曰：「今日畋，樂乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor entered the banner gate and exclaimed to those beside him, "Today's hunt—was it enjoyable?
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor passed through the banner gate, he asked his attendants, "Was today's hunt a pleasure?

sentences.zh: 世長曰：「陛下廢萬機，事遊獵，不滿十旬，未為樂也。」

translations.literal: Shichang said, "Your Majesty has set aside the myriad affairs of state to devote yourself to hunting. In less than a hundred days, this cannot yet be called enjoyment."
translations.idiomatic: Shichang said, "Your Majesty has set aside the myriad affairs of state for the chase. In less than a hundred days this can hardly count as pleasure."

sentences.zh: 帝色變，既而笑曰：「狂態發邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor's expression changed; then he laughed and said, "Has your wild manner broken out?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened, then he laughed and said, "Are you showing your wild streak again?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「為臣計則狂，為陛下計忠矣。」

translations.literal: He said, "By the reckoning of a subject it is wild; by the reckoning of Your Majesty it is loyal."
translations.idiomatic: Shichang said, "By a subject's measure it may be wild; by Your Majesty's measure it is loyalty."

sentences.zh: 時武功、郿新經突厥寇掠，鄉聚凋虛，帝將遂獵武功，世長諫曰：「突厥向盜劫人，陛下救恤之言未出口，又獵其地，殆百姓不堪所求。」

translations.literal: At that time Wugong and Mei had newly suffered Turkic raids and plunder; villages were depleted and empty. The Emperor was about to continue hunting at Wugong. Shichang remonstrated, saying, "The Turks have lately robbed and seized people. Your Majesty's words of relief and succor have not yet left your lips, yet you hunt in their land again—perhaps the common people cannot bear what is asked of them."
translations.idiomatic: Wugong and Mei had just been ravaged by Turkic raids, and the countryside lay wasted. When the emperor prepared to hunt on through Wugong, Shichang remonstrated: "The Turks have only lately been plundering your people. Your words of relief have scarcely been spoken, and already you would hunt their land again—the people can hardly endure what you demand of them."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 侍宴披香殿，酒酣，進曰：「此煬帝作邪？

translations.literal: Attending a banquet in the Poxiang Hall, when the wine was warm, he advanced and said, "Was this built by Emperor Yang?
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Poxiang Hall, when the wine had gone round, he stepped forward and asked, "Was this hall built by Emperor Yang?

sentences.zh: 何雕麗底此！」

translations.literal: How carved and splendid to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: How extravagantly carved and gilded it is!

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿好諫似直，然詐也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You love to remonstrate and seem straight, yet you are deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You love to remonstrate and play the honest man, yet you are being deceitful.

sentences.zh: 豈不知此殿我所營，乃詭雲煬帝邪？」

translations.literal: Do you not know that I built this hall myself, yet you falsely say it was Emperor Yang?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know that I built this hall myself—yet you pretend it was Emperor Yang's work?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣但見傾宮、鹿台，非受命聖人所為者。

translations.literal: He answered, "Your servant only sees a Tilted Palace and a Deer Terrace—works not of a sage who has received the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I see only another Tilted Palace, another Deer Terrace—nothing that a sage who has received Heaven's mandate would build.

sentences.zh: 陛下武功舊第，才蔽風雨，時以為足。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's old residence at Wugong barely kept off wind and rain, and at the time that was thought sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Your old house at Wugong barely kept out wind and rain, and in those days you thought it enough.

sentences.zh: 今天下厭隋之侈，以歸有道，陛下宜刈奢淫，復樸素。

translations.literal: Now the realm is weary of Sui extravagance and has turned to the Way. Your Majesty ought to cut down luxury and lewdness and return to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is weary of Sui excess and has turned to a ruler who holds the Way. Your Majesty ought to cut down luxury and restore plain living.

sentences.zh: 今乃即其宮加雕飾焉，欲易其亂，得乎？」

translations.literal: Yet now you take that very palace and add carving and ornament—wishing to change its disorder, can you succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you take that very palace and add carving and ornament—do you think you can end the disorder of the Sui that way?"

sentences.zh: 帝咨重其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor looked to him with weight and valued his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his words to heart.

sentences.zh: 曆陝州長史、天策府軍諮祭酒，引為學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Administrator of Shanzhou, Military Adviser and Libationer of the Heavenly Strategies Office, and was brought in as an academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as administrator of Shanzhou and military adviser and libationer in the Heavenly Strategies Office, and was appointed an academician.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，使突厥，與頡利爭禮，不屈，拒卻賂遺，朝廷壯之。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was sent to the Turks; he disputed ceremonial precedence with Jieli and would not yield, and refused bribes and gifts. The court admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was sent as envoy to the Turks. He contested ceremonial precedence with Jieli and would not yield, and he refused all bribes and gifts. The court took pride in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 出為巴州刺史，舟敗，溺死。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Bazhou; his boat was wrecked and he drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Bazhou, but his boat was wrecked and he drowned.

sentences.zh: 世長有機辯，淺於學，嗜酒，簡率無威儀。

translations.literal: Shichang had ready wit and argument, was shallow in learning, loved wine, and was plain and unceremonious without dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was quick-witted and sharp-tongued, shallow in scholarship, fond of wine, and plain in manner, without the dignified bearing of a statesman.

sentences.zh: 初在陝，邑裏犯法不能禁，乃引咎自撻於廛，五伯疾其詭，鞭之流血，世長不勝痛，呼而走，人笑其不情。

translations.literal: When he was first in Shan, he could not suppress lawbreaking in the district. He therefore took blame upon himself and flogged himself in the marketplace. The ward chiefs resented his affectation and whipped him until blood flowed. Shichang could not bear the pain, cried out, and ran away; people laughed at his lack of sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in Shanzhou, he could not stop crime in the district. He took the blame on himself and publicly flogged himself in the marketplace. The ward chiefs, disgusted by the show, whipped him until he bled. Unable to endure the pain, he cried out and fled; onlookers laughed at his insincerity.

sentences.zh: 子 良嗣

translations.literal: Son Liangsi
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangsi

sentences.zh: 子良嗣，高宗時為周王府司馬，王年少不法，良嗣數諫王，以法繩府官不職者，甚見尊憚。

translations.literal: Liangsi, in the Gaozong reign, was Military Adjutant of the Zhou King's Household. The prince was young and lawless; Liangsi repeatedly remonstrated with him and bound with the law those household officials who were derelict, and was greatly respected and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi served under Emperor Gaozong as military adjutant in the household of the Prince of Zhou. The prince was young and unruly; Liangsi repeatedly admonished him and disciplined negligent officials in the household by the book, and came to be greatly respected and feared.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，選荊州長史。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought him unusual and selected him as Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took note of him and appointed him administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宦者采怪竹江南，將蒔上苑，宦者所過縱暴，至荊，良嗣囚之，上書言狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent eunuchs to gather strange bamboo south of the Yangtze to plant in the imperial park. Wherever the eunuchs passed they indulged in violence. Reaching Jing, Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a memorial on the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs to collect exotic bamboo in the south for the imperial park. Wherever they went they abused their authority. When they reached Jingzhou, Liangsi had them arrested and reported their conduct to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔慰獎，取竹棄之。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict to comfort and reward him, and had the bamboo taken and discarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict commending him and ordered the bamboo thrown away.

sentences.zh: 徙雍州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時關內饑，人相食，良嗣政上嚴，每盜發，三日內必擒，號稱神明。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered famine and people ate one another. Liangsi's government was severe; whenever a theft occurred, the culprit was surely captured within three days, and he was called divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Famine then gripped Guanzhong and men ate one another. Liangsi governed with stern discipline: every theft reported was solved within three days, and people called his justice uncanny.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，遷冬官尚書，拜納言，封溫國公，留守西京，賞遇尤渥。

translations.literal: Early in the Chuigong reign he was promoted to Minister of the Winter Office, appointed Chief Counselor, enfeoffed as Duke of Wenguo, and left to guard the Western Capital; his rewards and favor were especially thick.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chuigong era he was made minister of the winter office and chief counselor, enfeoffed as Duke of Wenguo, and left to guard the western capital, where imperial favor toward him was especially generous.

sentences.zh: 尚方監裴匪躬案諸苑，建言鬻果蔬，儲利佐公上。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong inspected the various parks and proposed selling fruits and vegetables to store profit to assist the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Feigong, director of the palace workshops, inspected the imperial parks and proposed selling their fruits and vegetables to swell the public revenue.

sentences.zh: 良嗣曰：「公儀休一諸侯相，拔葵去織，未聞天子賣果蔬與人爭利。」

translations.literal: Liangsi said, "Gongyi Xiu, a single feudal lord's chancellor, uprooted melons and removed weaving—one has not heard of a Son of Heaven selling fruits and vegetables to contend for profit with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi said, "Gongyi Xiu, though only a feudal minister, uprooted his melons and stopped his wife's weaving rather than compete with the people. I have never heard of a Son of Heaven peddling garden produce for profit.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The plan was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Office and Third Rank, Equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left chancellor of the Wenchang Office and third rank, equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 遇薛懷義於朝，懷義偃蹇，良嗣怒，叱左右批其頰，曳去。

translations.literal: He encountered Xue Huaiyi at court; Huaiyi was insolent. Liangsi grew angry, ordered attendants to slap his cheeks, and had him dragged away.
translations.idiomatic: He met Xue Huaiyi at court; Huaiyi behaved with arrogant insolence. Liangsi flew into a rage, ordered his attendants to strike Huaiyi across the face, and had him dragged off.

sentences.zh: 武后聞之，戒曰：「第出入北門，彼南衙宰相行來，毋犯之。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu heard of it and warned him, saying, "Just go in and out by the north gate. Those southern-office chancellors come and go—do not offend them.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu heard of it, she warned him: "Use only the north gate from now on. The southern-office chancellors pass that way—do not provoke them.

sentences.zh: 載初元年，罷左相，加特進，仍知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zai Chu he was removed as Left Chancellor, given special advancement, and still directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zai Chu he was removed as left chancellor but given the rank of special advancement and continued to direct state affairs.

sentences.zh: 與韋方質素不平，方質坐事誅，引逮之。

translations.literal: He and Wei Fangzhi had long been on bad terms. When Fangzhi was executed for an offense, Liangsi was implicated and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wei Fangzhi had long been at odds. When Fangzhi was executed for a crime, Liangsi was implicated and arrested.

sentences.zh: 後辨其非，良嗣悸，謝不能興，輿還第，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: Later it was determined that he was not guilty. Liangsi was shaken, apologized but could not rise, was carried back to his residence, and died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When he was later cleared, Liangsi was so shaken that he could not rise to thank the court. He was carried home in a litter and died there at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔百官往吊，贈開府儀同三司、益州都督。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to go and mourn him; he was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Regional Commander of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed all officials to attend his funeral rites. He was posthumously honored as grand master of splendid happiness with the golden seal and as regional commander of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 始，良嗣為洛州長史，坐僚婿累，下徙冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Liangsi was Administrator of Luozhou, he was implicated through a son-in-law among his subordinates and demoted to Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Liangsi was administrator of Luozhou, he was implicated through a subordinate's son-in-law and demoted to governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 其人往謝，良嗣色泰定，曰：「初不聞有累。」

translations.literal: That man went to apologize; Liangsi's expression was calm and settled, and he said, "At first I did not hear that there was any implication.
translations.idiomatic: The man came to apologize. Liangsi remained perfectly calm and said, "I never heard that I was implicated in the first place.

sentences.zh: 在荊州時，州有河東寺，本蕭詧為兄河東王所建，良嗣曰：「江、漢間何與河東乎？」

translations.literal: When he was in Jingzhou, the prefecture had a Hedong Temple, originally built by Xiao Cha for his elder brother the Prince of Hedong. Liangsi said, "What has the region between the Yangtze and Han to do with Hedong?"
translations.idiomatic: While in Jingzhou he found a temple called Hedong, which Xiao Cha had built for his elder brother the Prince of Hedong. Liangsi said, "What has a place between the Yangtze and the Han to do with Hedong?"

sentences.zh: 奏易之，而當世恨其少學雲。

translations.literal: He memorialized to change the name, and men of the time resented his shallow learning.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to have the name changed, and contemporaries blamed his shallow learning."

sentences.zh: 子踐言，官太常丞，為酷吏所陷，死嶺南，削父爵，沒其家。

translations.literal: His son Jianyan was a Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was framed by a cruel official, died in Lingnan, his father's title was stripped, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianyan served as vice director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Framed by a cruel official, he died in exile in Lingnan; his father's title was revoked and the family property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，復贈司空，以踐言子務元襲爵，終邠王府長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, the post of Minister of Works was restored in gift; Jianyan's son Wuyuan inherited the title and ended as Chief Administrator of the Bin King's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong the family was posthumously honored again with the rank of minister of works; Jianyan's son Wuyuan inherited the title and ended his career as chief administrator of the household of the Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 從孫 弁

translations.literal: Grandnephew Bian
translations.idiomatic: His grandnephew Bian

sentences.zh: 從孫弁，字元容，擢進士，調奉天主簿。

translations.literal: The grandnephew Bian, style Yuangrong, passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Chief Clerk of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, a grandnephew of the family, style name Yuangrong, passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗出狩，而縣令計事在府，官屬皆惶恐，欲遁走。

translations.literal: When Dezong went out on campaign, the magistrate was away handling affairs at the prefectural seat; the officials were all fearful and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled the capital on campaign, the county magistrate was away at the prefectural seat on business, and the staff panicked and wanted to scatter.

sentences.zh: 弁曰：「昔肅宗幸靈武，至新平、安定，二太守坐伏匿，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Bian said, "Formerly when Suzong went to Lingwu, reaching Xinping and Anding, the two prefects were punished for concealing themselves and were beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "When Emperor Suzong went to Lingwu, the prefects of Xinping and Anding were executed for hiding themselves away. Do you know that story?

sentences.zh: 諸君知之乎？」

translations.literal: Do you gentlemen know this?
translations.idiomatic: Do you understand?

sentences.zh: 眾乃定。

translations.literal: The crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The staff steadied themselves.

sentences.zh: 車駕至，儲偫畢給，帝嘉之，試大理司直。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, stores and supplies were fully provided. The Emperor praised him and tested him as Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial train arrived, all provisions were ready. The emperor commended him and appointed him on probation as direct clerk in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 硃泚平，進監察御史，擢累倉部郎中，判度支案。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was pacified, he was promoted to Investigating Censor, then repeatedly advanced to Director of the Granary Office, and judged cases in the Directorate of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's rebellion was crushed, he was promoted to investigating censor, then rose through successive posts to director of the granary office, with responsibility for treasury affairs.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡死，帝召弁見延英，賜紫衣金魚，以度支郎中副知度支事，位郎中上。

translations.literal: When Pei Yanling died, the Emperor summoned Bian to an audience in the Yanying Hall, bestowed purple robes and the golden fish tally, and made him Director of the Treasury to assist in knowing treasury affairs, ranking above the director.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Yanling's death the emperor summoned Bian to the Yanying Hall, granted him purple robes and the golden fish tally, and appointed him director of the treasury to assist in managing fiscal affairs, with precedence over the regular director.

sentences.zh: 知度支有副自弁始。

translations.literal: The post of assistant in knowing treasury affairs began with Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The office of deputy director for treasury affairs began with Bian.

sentences.zh: 弁通學術，吏事精明，承延齡後，平賦緩役，略煩苛，人賴其寬。

translations.literal: Bian was versed in scholarship; in official matters he was sharp and clear. Following Yanling, he leveled levies and eased corvée, reduced troublesome severity, and the people relied on his leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was learned and skilled in administration. After Yanling he leveled taxes, eased labor service, and trimmed excessive severity; the people benefited from his moderation.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷戶部侍郎，判度支，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Households and judged the treasury; he was then changed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made vice minister of revenue with charge of treasury affairs, then transferred to grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 舊制，詹事位在太常宗正卿下，御史中丞竇參卑之，徙班河南、太原尹下。

translations.literal: By old regulation the Grand Mentor's rank was below the Directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan. The Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Can looked down on it and moved his place in court below the Governors of Henan and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom the grand mentor ranked below the directors of the courts of imperial sacrifices and of the imperial clan. Vice censor-in-chief Dou Can slighted the post and had Bian's court rank placed below the governors of Henan and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 弁造朝，輒就舊著，有司疑詰，紿曰：「我已白宰相，復舊班。」

translations.literal: When Bian came to court he always took his old place. The relevant offices questioned him in doubt; he deceived them, saying, "I have already informed the chancellor to restore the old order of court.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian attended court he always took his former place. When the officials questioned him, he lied and said, "I have already told the chancellor to restore my old rank.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史鄒儒立劾奏，待罪金吾，有詔原罪。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Zou Ruli memorialized in impeachment; he awaited punishment in the Golden Crow Guard. An edict pardoned the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant censor Zou Ruli impeached him; Bian awaited punishment in the Golden Crow Guard, but an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 坐前以腐粟給邊，貶汀州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was punished for earlier having supplied rotten grain to the frontier and was demoted to Army Adjutant for Household Registration in Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later punished for having once supplied spoiled grain to the frontier armies and was demoted to army adjutant for household registration in Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，兄袞為贊善大夫，冕京兆士曹參軍，以弁故，貶袞永州，冕信州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Gun was Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Mian was a Staff Officer in the Jingzhao Commandery. Because of Bian, Gun was demoted to Yongzhou and Mian to Army Adjutant for Household Registration in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brothers Gun and Mian served as mentor of the heir apparent and as a staff officer in the Jingzhao commandery. Because of Bian's offense, Gun was demoted to Yongzhou and Mian to army adjutant in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 袞年老，瞑不能視，帝閔之，聽還。

translations.literal: Gun was old and blind and could not see; the Emperor pitied him and permitted him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was elderly and had gone blind; the emperor took pity on him and allowed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 又有稱冕才者，帝悔不用，而袞以老先還，重追冕。

translations.literal: There were also those who praised Mian's talent; the Emperor regretted not having employed him. But because Gun returned first on account of age, he again summoned Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Others praised Mian's ability, and the emperor regretted not having used him. Yet because Gun had already been sent home on account of age, the court turned again to Mian.

sentences.zh: 更問大臣昆弟可任者，左右以王紹之兄紓、韓皋之兄群對。

translations.literal: He again asked which brothers of great ministers were fit for employment; those beside him answered with Wang Shaozhi's elder brother Shu and Han Gao's elder brother Qun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked which brothers of senior ministers might serve. His attendants named Wang Shaozhi's elder brother Shu and Han Gao's elder brother Qun.

sentences.zh: 帝乃擢紓右補闕，群考功員外郎，冕遂不復用。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon promoted Shu to Right Remonstrator and Qun to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; Mian was then never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then promoted Shu to right remonstrator and Qun to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Mian was never employed again.

sentences.zh: 數年，起弁為滁州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: After several years he was recalled and made Governor of Chuzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Bian was recalled and appointed governor of Chuzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 弁聚書至二萬卷，手自讎定，當時稱與秘府將。

translations.literal: Bian collected books to the number of twenty thousand scrolls, collated them with his own hand, and men of the time said they would rank with the imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed a library of twenty thousand scrolls and collated them himself; contemporaries said it nearly matched the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 弁之判度支，方大旱，州縣有逋米，斷貞元八年以前，凡三百八十萬斛，人亡數在，弁奏請出以貸貧民，至秋而償，詔可。

translations.literal: When Bian judged treasury affairs, there was a great drought. In the prefectures and districts there was grain in arrears; cutting off years before the eighth year of Zhenyuan, the total was 3,800,000 hu. Though the persons were dead, the amounts remained. Bian memorialized to release it on loan to the poor, to be repaid by autumn. An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: While Bian oversaw treasury affairs a severe drought struck. Counties and prefectures held unpaid grain arrears dating before the eighth year of Zhenyuan—some 3,800,000 hu in all. Though many debtors were dead, the accounts remained. Bian memorialized to lend this grain to the poor for repayment by autumn, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 當時譏其罔君雲。

translations.literal: At the time he was criticized for deceiving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries criticized the scheme as deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 韋雲起

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi

sentences.zh: 韋雲起，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi was a native of Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，以明經補符璽直長。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of the Sui, through the Mingjing examination he was appointed Direct Clerk of Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Kaihuang era he passed the classics examination and was appointed direct clerk of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事文帝前，帝曰：「外事不便，可言之。」

translations.literal: Once when he was reporting affairs before Emperor Wen, the Emperor said, "If anything outside is inconvenient, you may speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while reporting to Emperor Wen, he was told, "If anything in public affairs is amiss, speak freely.

sentences.zh: 時兵部侍郎柳述侍，雲起即奏：「述性豪侈，未嘗更事，特緣主婿私，握兵要，議者謂陛下官不擇賢，此不便者。」

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of War Liu Shu attended. Yunqi immediately memorialized, "Shu is by nature extravagant and has never handled affairs. He holds the military keys solely through private ties as the emperor's son-in-law. Critics say Your Majesty does not choose the worthy for office—this is what is inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Liu Shu stood in attendance. Yunqi immediately said, "Shu is extravagant by nature and has never managed affairs. He holds military power only because he is the emperor's son-in-law. Critics say Your Majesty appoints by favor rather than merit—that is the real inconvenience."

sentences.zh: 帝顧述曰：「雲起言，而藥石也，可師之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to Shu and said, "Yunqi's words are medicine and stone—you may take him as a teacher."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Shu and said, "Yunqi speaks harsh truth like medicine and whetstone. You should learn from him."

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，詔百官舉所知，述舉雲起通事舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Renshou, an edict ordered all officials to recommend those they knew; Shu recommended Yunqi as Master of Ceremonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era an edict called on officials to recommend talent they knew; Shu nominated Yunqi for master of ceremonial affairs.

sentences.zh: 大業初，改謁者。

translations.literal: Early in Daye he was changed to Master of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era he was made master of guests.

sentences.zh: 建言：「今朝廷多山東人，自作門戶，附下罔上，為朋黨。

translations.literal: He proposed, "Now the court has many men from east of the mountains who form their own factions, attach to subordinates and deceive superiors, and make cliques.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The court is now full of men from east of the mountains who form private factions, curry favor below and deceive above, and build cliques.

sentences.zh: 不抑其端，必亂政。」

translations.literal: If their beginnings are not checked, government will surely be thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Unless this is checked at the root, government will fall into chaos.

sentences.zh: 因條陳奸狀。

translations.literal: He thereupon itemized their wicked conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed their offenses in detail.

sentences.zh: 煬帝屬大理推究，於是左丞郎蔚之、司隸別駕郎楚之等皆坐免。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang charged the Court of Judicial Review to investigate. Thereupon Left Assistant Minister Lang Weizhi, Vice Director of the Metropolitan Inspectorate Lang Chuzhi, and others were all punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered the Court of Judicial Review to investigate. Left assistant minister Lang Weizhi, vice director of the metropolitan inspectorate Lang Chuzhi, and others were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會契丹寇營州，詔雲起護突厥兵討之，啟民可汗以二萬騎受節度。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided Yingzhou, an edict ordered Yunqi to command Turkic troops to attack them; Qimin Khan placed twenty thousand horsemen under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Yingzhou, Yunqi was ordered to lead Turkic forces against them; Qimin Khan placed twenty thousand cavalry under his command.

sentences.zh: 雲起使離為二十屯，屯相聯絡，四道並引，令曰：「鼓而行，角而止，非公使，毋走馬。」

translations.literal: Yunqi had them split into twenty encampments linked in succession, advancing by four routes together, and ordered, "At drum, march; at horn, halt. Without the envoy's command, no one rides at full gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi divided the force into twenty linked encampments advancing along four routes and issued orders: "March at the drum, halt at the horn. No one may gallop without the envoy's command.

sentences.zh: 三喻五復之。

translations.literal: He explained this three times and repeated it five times.
translations.idiomatic: He explained the orders three times and repeated them five times over.

sentences.zh: 既而紇斤一人犯令，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: Soon afterward one Hejin man violated the order and was immediately beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When one Hejin tribesman broke the rule, Yunqi had him beheaded at once as an example.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥酋長入謁者，皆膝而進，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turkic chiefs who came to audience all advanced on their knees and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every Turkic chief who came before him advanced on his knees and dared not raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 始，契丹事突厥無間，且不虞雲起至。

translations.literal: At first the Khitan had served the Turks without interruption and did not expect Yunqi to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had long served the Turks without a break and never expected Yunqi to appear.

sentences.zh: 既入境，使突厥紿雲詣柳城與高麗市易，敢言有隋使在者斬。

translations.literal: After entering their territory, he had the Turks deceive them with the story that they were going to Liucheng to trade with Goguryeo, and ordered that anyone who spoke of a Sui envoy being present be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Khitan territory he had the Turks spread word that they were bound for Liucheng to trade with Goguryeo, and decreed death for anyone who mentioned a Sui envoy.

sentences.zh: 契丹不疑。

translations.literal: The Khitan did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 因引而南，過賊營百里，夜還陣，以遲明掩擊之，獲契丹男女四萬，以女子及畜產半賜突厥，男子悉殺之，以餘眾還。

translations.literal: He therefore led them south, passed the enemy camp by a hundred li, returned to formation at night, and at daybreak launched a surprise attack. He took forty thousand Khitan men and women; half the women and livestock he gave to the Turks, all the men he killed outright, and with the remainder he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south past the enemy camp by a hundred li, returned to his lines by night, and at dawn struck by surprise. He captured forty thousand Khitan men and women, gave half the women and livestock to the Turks, killed all the men, and marched home with the rest.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，會百官於廷，曰：「雲起將突厥兵平契丹，以奇用師，有文武才，朕自舉之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and assembled the hundred officials in court, saying, "Yunqi led Turkic troops to pacify the Khitan, employing troops by stratagem. He has both civil and military talent—I raised him up myself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told the assembled officials, "Yunqi led the Turks to crush the Khitan by unconventional tactics. He has both civil and military gifts—I chose him myself.

sentences.zh: 拜治書御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi was appointed imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 因劾奏：「內史侍郎虞世基、御史大夫裴蘊怙寵妨命，四方有變不以聞，聞不以實。

translations.literal: He thereupon impeached and memorialized, "Inner Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun rely on favor and obstruct orders. When disturbances arise in the four quarters they do not report them; when they report, they do not report truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Inner Secretariat vice director Yu Shiji and censor-in-chief Pei Yun for abusing imperial favor and obstructing orders—for concealing unrest in the realm and, when they did report, reporting falsely.

sentences.zh: 朝議少賊，不多發兵，官兵少，賊眾，數見敗北，賊氣日張。

translations.literal: Court deliberations underestimated the rebels and did not send out many troops. Government troops were few, rebels many; defeat followed defeat and rebel morale grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberations underestimated the rebels and sent too few troops; government forces were outnumbered, defeats piled up, and rebel morale rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 請付有司案罪。」

translations.literal: I ask that they be handed to the relevant offices to investigate their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be handed over for criminal investigation.

sentences.zh: 大理卿鄭善果奏：「雲起訾大臣，毀朝政，所言不情。」

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Shanguo memorialized, "Yunqi slanders great ministers and defames court governance; what he says is not reasonable."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Shanguo replied that Yunqi was slandering senior ministers, defaming the court, and speaking without cause.

sentences.zh: 貶大理司直。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi was demoted to direct clerk in the same court.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，請告歸。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to Jiangdu, Yunqi requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, Yunqi asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，上謁長樂宮，授司農卿、陽城縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes, Yunqi presented himself at Changle Palace and was appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and Duke of Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes, Yunqi presented himself at Changle Palace and was made director of agriculture and Duke of Yangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 武德初，進上開府儀同三司，判農圃監。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and judged the Directorate of Gardens and Parks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness with the golden seal and placed in charge of the directorate of gardens and parks.

sentences.zh: 時議討王世充，雲起上言：「京師初平，人未堅附，百姓流離，仍歲無年。

translations.literal: At the time there was deliberation on attacking Wang Shichong. Yunqi submitted, "The capital has only just been pacified; the people are not yet firmly attached. The common people are displaced and wandering, and year after year there is no harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated attacking Wang Shichong, Yunqi argued: "The capital has only just been pacified and the people are not yet firmly loyal. The populace is displaced, and harvests have failed year after year.

sentences.zh: 盩厔〗司竹、藍田谷口，盜賊群屯。

translations.literal: At Zhoushi, Sizhu, and the valley mouths of Lantian, bandits gather in groups.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhoushi, Sizhu, and the valley mouths of Lantian, bandits gather in bands.

sentences.zh: 京都椎剽，乘夜竊發。

translations.literal: In the capital there is violent robbery; they strike by night in secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital violent robbery breaks out under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 重以梁師都嫁情北胡，陰計內鈔，為腹心患。

translations.literal: Added to this, Liang Shidu has married his interests to the northern barbarians and plots secretly for internal raids—a danger at the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liang Shidu has allied himself with the northern tribes and plots raids from within—a danger at our very core.

sentences.zh: 釋此不圖，而窺兵函、洛，奸人乘虛，一旦有變，禍且不細。

translations.literal: To set aside planning for this and instead cast military eyes on Hangu and Luoyang—when villains seize the void, if change comes in a morning, the disaster will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore these threats and instead fix our armies on Hangu and Luoyang is to invite troublemakers to strike at our weakness. If crisis comes overnight, the disaster will be grave.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為不若戢兵務農，須關中妥安，士氣餘飽，然議討伐，一舉可定。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks it would be better to sheath the troops and devote effort to agriculture. Only when Guanzhong is settled and secure, when morale is restored and bellies full, should we then deliberate on campaigning—then one stroke can settle it.
translations.idiomatic: I believe it would be wiser to halt military campaigns and devote ourselves to agriculture. Once Guanzhong is secure and the people fed and rested, then we may campaign—and victory will come in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，詔總豳、寧以北九洲兵禦之，得一切便宜。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded, an edict ordered him to command the troops of the nine prefectures north of Bin and Ning to resist them, with full discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, he was ordered to command the armies of the nine prefectures north of Bin and Ning, with full discretionary power.

sentences.zh: 改遂州都督、益州行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Regional Commander of Suizhou and Minister of War of the Yizhou Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regional commander of Suizhou and minister of war on the Yizhou mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時僕射竇軌數奏生獠反，冀得集兵以威眾，雲起數持掣，軌宣言雲起通賊營私，由是始隙。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Dou Gui repeatedly memorialized that the raw tribes were in revolt, hoping to gather troops to awe the masses. Yunqi repeatedly restrained him. Gui publicly declared that Yunqi communicated with rebels and sought private gain, and from this their rift began.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Dou Gui repeatedly reported rebellions among the tribal peoples, hoping to gather troops and awe the region. Yunqi repeatedly blocked him. Gui then publicly accused Yunqi of colluding with rebels for private gain, and a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 雲起弟慶儉、慶嗣事隱太子。

translations.literal: Yunqi's younger brothers Qingjian and Qingsi served the Hidden Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi's younger brothers Qingjian and Qingsi served the hidden heir.

sentences.zh: 太子死，詔軌息馳驛報。

translations.literal: When the Heir died, an edict ordered Gui's son to ride post-horses and report.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir died, an edict ordered Gui's son to ride post relays and report the news.

sentences.zh: 軌疑雲起有變，陰設備，乃告之。

translations.literal: Gui suspected Yunqi of plotting change, secretly made preparations, and then informed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui suspected Yunqi of plotting rebellion, secretly made preparations, and then confronted him.

sentences.zh: 雲起不信，曰：「詔安在？」

translations.literal: Yunqi did not believe it and said, "Where is the edict?
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi refused to believe it and demanded, "Where is the edict?

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「公建成黨，今不奉詔，反明矣。」

translations.literal: Gui said, "Sir, you are of Jiancheng's faction. Now you do not obey the edict—rebellion is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "You are of Jiancheng's faction. Your refusal to obey the edict proves rebellion plainly enough."

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Yunqi killed.

sentences.zh: 初，雲起師太學博士王頗，每歎曰：「韋生識悟，富貴可自致；

translations.literal: Earlier Yunqi had studied under Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Po. Wang would sigh and say, "Student Wei has insight and understanding; wealth and honor he can attain himself;
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi had studied under imperial academy erudite Wang Po, who once sighed and said, "Young Wei has keen insight and can win wealth and honor for himself;

sentences.zh: 然疾惡甚，恐不得死。」

translations.literal: yet he hates evil intensely—I fear he will not die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: but he hates wickedness too fiercely—I fear he will not die in his bed.

sentences.zh: 訖如言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 孫方質，光宅初為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，遷地官尚書。

translations.literal: Fang Zhi, his grandson, early in Guangzhai was Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Equal in Court Deliberation with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, then transferred to Minister of the Earth Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Fang Zhi, early in the Guangzhai era, served as vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and equal in court deliberation, then was made minister of the earth office.

sentences.zh: 嘗屬疾，武承嗣兄弟往候，方質據床自若。

translations.literal: Once when he was ill, Wu Chengsi and his brothers came to inquire after him; Fang Zhi sat on his bed at ease as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while ill, he received a visit from Wu Chengsi and his brothers and remained seated on his bed without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「倨見權貴，且速禍。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "To be arrogant before the powerful will soon bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "To show such arrogance toward the powerful will bring disaster quickly.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「吉凶命也，丈夫豈能折節近戚以苟免邪？」

translations.literal: He answered, "Fortune and misfortune are fate. How can a man bend his integrity to draw near to kin by marriage merely to escape harm?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Fortune and misfortune are fate. Should a man bend his spine to court imperial in-laws merely to save his skin?"

sentences.zh: 俄為酷吏所陷，流死儋州，沒其家。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed by a cruel official, exiled and died in Danzhou, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a cruel official framed him; he died in exile in Danzhou and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，復官爵。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong his offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era his offices and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽

translations.literal: Sun Fuga
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuga

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Sun Fuga was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuga was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，以小史累勞補萬年縣法曹。

translations.literal: He served the Sui; through accumulated merit as a minor clerk he was appointed Legal Officer of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose through minor clerk posts by accumulated merit to legal officer of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 高祖武德初，上言三事。

translations.literal: Early in Gaozu's Wude reign he submitted a memorial on three matters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's Wude reign he submitted a memorial on three matters.

sentences.zh: 其一：臣聞「天子有爭臣，雖無道不失其天下」。

translations.literal: First: I have heard, “If the Son of Heaven has remonstrating ministers, even if he lacks the Way, he will not lose his realm.”
translations.idiomatic: First: I have heard, “If the Son of Heaven has remonstrating ministers, even if he lacks the Way, he will not lose his realm.”

sentences.zh: 隋失天下者何？

translations.literal: Why did the Sui lose the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Why did the Sui lose the realm?

sentences.zh: 不聞其過也。

translations.literal: Because it did not hear of its faults.
translations.idiomatic: Because it did not hear of its faults.

sentences.zh: 方自謂功德盛五帝、邁三王，窮侈極欲，使天下士肝腦塗地，戶口殫耗、盜賊日滋。

translations.literal: It was just then claiming that its achievements and virtue surpassed the Five Emperors and exceeded the Three Kings, while it exhausted extravagance and indulged desire, making the officers of the realm spill their brains on the ground, households and population waste away, and bandits daily multiply.
translations.idiomatic: It was just then claiming that its achievements and virtue surpassed the Five Emperors and exceeded the Three Kings, while it exhausted extravagance and indulged desire, making the officers of the realm spill their brains on the ground, households and population waste away, and bandits daily multiply.

sentences.zh: 當時非無直言之臣，卒不聞悟者，君不受諫，而臣不敢告之也。

translations.literal: At the time, it was not that there were no ministers who spoke straight, but in the end no awakening was heard, because the ruler did not accept remonstrance and ministers did not dare tell him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, it was not that there were no ministers who spoke straight, but in the end no awakening was heard, because the ruler did not accept remonstrance and ministers did not dare tell him.

sentences.zh: 向使開不諱之路，官賢授能，賞罰時當，人人樂業，誰能搖亂者乎？

translations.literal: If he had opened the way for speech without taboo, appointed the worthy and entrusted the able, and made rewards and punishments timely and proper, so that everyone was content in his work, who could have shaken or disturbed him?
translations.idiomatic: If he had opened the way for speech without taboo, appointed the worthy and entrusted the able, and made rewards and punishments timely and proper, so that everyone was content in his work, who could have shaken or disturbed him?

sentences.zh: 陛下舉晉陽，天下回應，計不旋跬，大業以成。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty rose at Jinyang, the realm responded, and before the plan had turned even half a step, the great enterprise was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty rose at Jinyang, the realm responded, and before the plan had turned even half a step, the great enterprise was complete.

sentences.zh: 勿以得天下之易，而忘隋失之不難也。

translations.literal: Do not, because gaining the realm was easy, forget that the Sui lost it without difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Do not, because gaining the realm was easy, forget that the Sui lost it without difficulty.

sentences.zh: 天子動則左史書之，言則右史書之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven moves, the left historian records it; when he speaks, the right historian records it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven moves, the left historian records it; when he speaks, the right historian records it.

sentences.zh: 凡搜狩當順四時，不可妄動。

translations.literal: All hunting should follow the four seasons and must not be undertaken recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: All hunting should follow the four seasons and must not be undertaken recklessly.

sentences.zh: 且陛下即位之明日，有獻鷂者，不卻而受，此前世弊事，奈何行之？

translations.literal: Moreover, the day after Your Majesty took the throne, someone offered a sparrowhawk, and you accepted it instead of refusing it. This is an abuse of former ages; how can it be practiced?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the day after Your Majesty took the throne, someone offered a sparrowhawk, and you accepted it instead of refusing it. This is an abuse of former ages; how can it be practiced?

sentences.zh: 相國參軍事盧牟子獻琵琶，長安丞張安道獻弓矢，並被賚賞。

translations.literal: Lu Mouzi, staff officer to the minister of state, offered a pipa, and Zhang Andao, assistant magistrate of Chang’an, offered bows and arrows, and both received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mouzi, staff officer to the minister of state, offered a pipa, and Zhang Andao, assistant magistrate of Chang’an, offered bows and arrows, and both received rewards.

sentences.zh: 以率土之富，何索不致，豈少此物哉？

translations.literal: With the wealth of all the land, what could be sought and not obtained? Can there be any shortage of such things?
translations.idiomatic: With the wealth of all the land, what could be sought and not obtained? Can there be any shortage of such things?

sentences.zh: 其二：百戲散樂，本非正聲，隋末始見崇用，此謂淫風，不得不變。

translations.literal: Second: the hundred entertainments and scattered music are not orthodox sound. Late in the Sui they began to be honored and used—this is what is called lewd custom, and it cannot but be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Second: variety shows and scattered music are not proper court music. Only late in the Sui were they elevated—this is licentious fashion and must be changed.

sentences.zh: 近太常假民裙襦五百稱，以衣妓工，待玄武門遊戲。

translations.literal: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed five hundred sets of commoners' skirts and jackets to clothe female performers, awaiting games at the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed five hundred sets of commoners' clothing to dress female performers for entertainments at the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 臣以為非詒子孫之謀。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks this is not planning that will bring blessing to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: I do not believe this serves the welfare of your descendants.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「放鄭聲，遠佞人。」

translations.literal: The tradition says, "Banish the music of Zheng and keep flatterers at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Banish the music of Zheng and keep flatterers at a distance.

sentences.zh: 今散妓者，匪《韶》匪《夏》，請並廢之，以復雅正。

translations.literal: Now the scattered female performers are neither the Shao nor the Xia. I ask that they all be abolished to restore elegant orthodoxy.
translations.idiomatic: Today's scattered performers are neither Shao nor Xia music. I ask that they all be abolished so court music may return to proper standards."

sentences.zh: 其三：臣聞「性相近，習相遠」。

translations.literal: Third: Your servant has heard, "By nature men are close together; by practice they grow far apart."
translations.idiomatic: Third: I have heard that natures are alike at birth but diverge through habit.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子諸王左右執事，不可不擇。

translations.literal: Now the attendants and executors at the left hand of the Heir Apparent and the princes cannot but be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants and staff around the crown prince and the imperial princes must be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 大抵不義無賴及馳騁射獵歌舞聲色慢遊之人，止可悅耳目，備驅馳，至拾遺補闕，決不能也。

translations.literal: Generally, the unrighteous and the worthless, and those who gallop in hunting, archery, song, dance, sensual sound and color, and idle roaming—such men may only please the ears and eyes and serve for running errands. As for picking up omissions and supplying deficiencies, they absolutely cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: Men who are unprincipled rogues, or who devote themselves to hunting, archery, song, dance, sensual pleasures, and idle roaming, may amuse the senses and run errands—but they can never remedy omissions or supply what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 泛觀前世，子姓不克孝，兄弟不克友，莫不由左右亂之。

translations.literal: Broadly viewing former ages, when sons and clansmen could not achieve filial piety and brothers could not achieve friendship, none was not because those at their left hand threw them into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Looking broadly at past ages, whenever sons failed in filial piety and brothers failed in fraternity, the fault lay with corrupt attendants.

sentences.zh: 願選賢才，澄僚友之選。

translations.literal: I wish that worthy talent be selected and the choice of colleagues and friends be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that worthy men be chosen and the selection of companions be purified."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，即詔：「周、隋之晚，忠臣結舌，是謂一言喪邦者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and immediately issued an edict: "In the late Zhou and Sui, loyal ministers sealed their tongues—this is what is called losing the state in a single word.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and at once issued an edict: "In the late Zhou and Sui loyal ministers dared not speak—that is how a state can be lost in a single word.

sentences.zh: 朕惟寡德，不能性與天道，然冀弼諧以輔不逮，而群公卿士罕進直言。

translations.literal: We alone lack virtue and cannot make our nature one with Heaven's Way, yet We hope for harmony in assistance to supply Our shortcomings, while the host of dukes, ministers, and scholars rarely advance straight words.
translations.idiomatic: I know my virtue is slight and I cannot align my nature with Heaven's Way, yet I look to my ministers to supply what I lack—while you rarely offer honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏伽至誠慷慨，據義懇切，指朕失無所諱。

translations.literal: Fuga is utterly sincere and generous, holds to righteousness earnestly and urgently, and points out Our faults without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Fuga has spoken with utmost sincerity and boldness, upholding righteousness without reserve and pointing out my faults openly.

sentences.zh: 其以伏伽為治書侍御史，賜帛三百匹。」

translations.literal: Let Fuga be made Attending Imperial Censor and granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Fuga attending imperial censor and grant him three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，帝受禪，伏伽最先諫，帝欲盡下情，故不次見拔，以示群臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Emperor received the abdication, Fuga was the first to remonstrate. The Emperor wished to exhaust the feelings of those below, and therefore promoted him out of turn to show the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first accepted the abdication, Fuga was the first to remonstrate with him. Wishing to encourage frank counsel from below, the emperor promoted him out of turn as an example to the court.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍興賦斂重，伏伽數請厘損。

translations.literal: At that time, with military campaigns arising, levies and collections were heavy; Fuga repeatedly requested reduction and relief.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military campaigns had made taxes heavy; Fuga repeatedly asked that levies be reduced.

sentences.zh: 帝語裴寂曰：「隋為無道，主驕於上，臣諂於下，下上蔽蒙，至身死匹夫手，寧不痛哉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Pei Ji, "The Sui was without the Way: the ruler was arrogant above, ministers flattered below, lower and upper obscured one another, until he died by a commoner's hand—how could it not pain one!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Pei Ji, "The Sui lost the Way: the ruler grew arrogant above while ministers flattered below, each side deceiving the other, until the emperor died at a commoner's hand—how painful a lesson that is!

sentences.zh: 我今不然，平亂責武臣，守成責儒臣，程能付事，以佐不逮；

translations.literal: I am not so now: for pacifying disorder I charge military ministers, for preserving the achievement I charge Confucian ministers, assign tasks according to capacity, to assist where I fall short;
translations.idiomatic: I will not repeat that error. I charge military men with pacifying chaos and scholars with preserving peace, assigning tasks by ability to supply what I lack;

sentences.zh: 虛心盡下，冀聞嘉言。

translations.literal: with an open mind I exhaust the feelings of those below, hoping to hear excellent words.
translations.idiomatic: and I open my mind to those below, hoping to hear good counsel.

sentences.zh: 若李綱、孫伏伽，可謂誼臣矣。

translations.literal: Men like Li Gang and Sun Fuga may be called righteous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Li Gang and Sun Fuga are the sort of righteous ministers I seek.

sentences.zh: 俯首噤默，豈朕所望哉？」

translations.literal: To bow the head and seal the tongue—is that what We hope for?"
translations.idiomatic: But if you bow your heads in silence, what use are you to me?"

sentences.zh: 東都平，大赦天下，又欲責賊支黨，悉流徙惡地。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, a great amnesty was proclaimed for the realm. The Emperor again wished to punish the branches and factions of the rebels and exile them all to evil lands.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern capital was pacified, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty, then planned to punish the rebel factions and exile them all to harsh regions.

sentences.zh: 伏伽諫曰：「臣聞王者無戲言，《書》稱'爾無不信，朕不食言'，言之不可不慎也。

translations.literal: Fuga remonstrated, saying, "Your servant has heard that a king has no jesting words. The Documents says, 'Do not be unbelieving; I will not eat my words'—speech cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Fuga remonstrated: "I have heard that a king must not speak in jest. The Documents says, 'Do not be unbelieving; I will not eat my words.' A ruler's words must be weighed with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 陛下制詔曰：'常赦不免，皆原之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's edict declared, 'Those whom regular amnesties do not exempt—all are pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Your edict declared, 'Even those whom ordinary amnesties would not spare—all are pardoned.'

sentences.zh: '此非直赦有罪，是亦與天下更新辭也。

translations.literal: This is not merely pardoning the guilty; it is also renewing the covenant with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This was not merely pardoning criminals; it was renewing the covenant with the realm.

sentences.zh: 世充、建德所部，赦後乃欲流徙。

translations.literal: The followers of Shichong and Jiande—after the amnesty You now wish to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, after the amnesty, you would exile the followers of Shichong and Jiande.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：'殲厥渠魁，憚從罔治。

translations.literal: The Documents says, 'Destroy the ringleaders; accomplices go unpunished.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'Destroy the ringleaders; spare the followers.'

sentences.zh: '渠魁尚免，憚從何辜？

translations.literal: If the ringleaders are still spared, what crime have the accomplices?
translations.idiomatic: If the leaders themselves are spared, what crime have their followers committed?

sentences.zh: 且蹠狗吠堯，吠非其主。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Zhi's dog barked at Yao, it barked not at its own master.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when Robber Zhi's dog barked at Yao, it barked at the wrong master.

sentences.zh: 今與陛下結髮雅故，往為賊臣，彼豈忘陛下哉，壅隔故也。

translations.literal: Now they have been Your Majesty's close companions since youth; formerly they were rebel ministers—how could they forget Your Majesty? They were cut off by obstruction, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Many were your old companions since youth who later served rebel lords. Do you think they have forgotten you? They were cut off by circumstance, that is all.

sentences.zh: 至疏者安得而罪之？

translations.literal: How can the most distant be charged with crime?
translations.idiomatic: How can the least involved be punished for it?

sentences.zh: 由古以來，何始無君，然止稱堯、舜者，何也？

translations.literal: From antiquity until now, when was there ever no ruler? Yet only Yao and Shun are named—why?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity there has never been an age without rulers—yet only Yao and Shun are praised. Why?

sentences.zh: 直由善名難得也。

translations.literal: Simply because a good name is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Simply because a good name is hard to earn.

sentences.zh: 昔天下未平，容應機制變。

translations.literal: Formerly, when the realm was not yet pacified, one might accommodate opportune change.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was still unsettled, flexibility was permissible.

sentences.zh: 今四方已定，設法須與人共之。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are settled; in establishing law one must share it with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the four quarters are settled, laws must be shared with the people.

sentences.zh: 法者陛下自作，須自守之，使天下百姓信而畏也。

translations.literal: The law is what Your Majesty himself made; You must yourself keep it, so that the common people of the realm trust and fear it.
translations.idiomatic: The law is what Your Majesty himself made; you must keep it yourself so that the people trust and fear it.

sentences.zh: 自為無信，欲人之信，豈可得哉？

translations.literal: If one is oneself without trustworthiness, yet wishes others to trust—how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If you yourself break faith, how can you expect others to trust you?

sentences.zh: 賞罰之行，無貴賤親疏，惟義所在。

translations.literal: In the execution of rewards and punishments, there is no noble or base, near or far—only where righteousness lies.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments must know no rank or kinship—only where justice lies.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為賊党於赦當免者，雖甚無狀，宜一切加原，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that among the rebel factions, those who ought to be spared by the amnesty, however utterly without propriety, should all be further pardoned—then the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that all rebel followers who ought to be covered by the amnesty, however deplorable their conduct, should be fully pardoned. The realm would be the happier for it.

sentences.zh: 又表置諫官。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to establish remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to establish remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 帝皆欽納。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted all with respect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all his proposals with respect.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，封樂安縣男，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Fuga was enfeoffed as county baron of Le’an and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Fuga was enfeoffed as county baron of Le’an and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 帝數出馳射，伏伽諫曰：「臣聞天子之居，禁衛九重，出也警，入也蹕，非直尊其居處，為社稷生人計也。

translations.literal: The emperor often went out riding and shooting, and Fuga remonstrated, “I have heard that where the Son of Heaven dwells, the forbidden guards are ninefold; when he goes out, warnings are given, and when he enters, the roads are cleared. This is not merely to honor his dwelling and movements, but is a plan for the altars of state and the living people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often went out riding and shooting, and Fuga remonstrated, “I have heard that where the Son of Heaven dwells, the forbidden guards are ninefold; when he goes out, warnings are given, and when he enters, the roads are cleared. This is not merely to honor his dwelling and movements, but is a plan for the altars of state and the living people.

sentences.zh: 比聞陛下走馬射帖，娛悅群臣，殆非所以導養聖躬、垂憲後代，此直少年諸王務耳，安得既為天子，尚行之乎？

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that Your Majesty races horses and shoots targets to entertain and delight the assembled ministers. This is hardly the way to guide and nourish the sage person or leave a model for later generations. These are only the pursuits of young princes; how can you, having become Son of Heaven, still practice them?
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have heard that Your Majesty races horses and shoots targets to entertain and delight the assembled ministers. This is hardly the way to guide and nourish the sage person or leave a model for later generations. These are only the pursuits of young princes; how can you, having become Son of Heaven, still practice them?

sentences.zh: 竊為陛下不取。」

translations.literal: Privately, I do not approve of this for Your Majesty.”
translations.idiomatic: Privately, I do not approve of this for Your Majesty.”

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「卿能言朕失，朕能改之，天下庶有瘳乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said, “You can speak of my faults, and I can correct them. Perhaps the realm may have some recovery!”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, “You can speak of my faults, and I can correct them. Perhaps the realm may have some recovery!”

sentences.zh: 後坐奏囚失，免官。

translations.literal: Later, he was implicated in an erroneous memorial about prisoners and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, he was implicated in an erroneous memorial about prisoners and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 起為刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Langzhong in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Langzhong in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時司農市木橦，倍直與民，右丞韋悰劾吏隱沒，事下大理訊鞫。

translations.literal: At that time, the Court of the Imperial Granaries purchased wooden posts and paid the people double the price. Right Vice Director Wei Cong impeached officials for concealment and embezzlement, and the matter was sent down to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the Court of the Imperial Granaries purchased wooden posts and paid the people double the price. Right Vice Director Wei Cong impeached officials for concealment and embezzlement, and the matter was sent down to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 伏伽曰：「緣官市貴，故民直賤。

translations.literal: Fuga said, “Because the government purchase price was high, the people’s price was low.
translations.idiomatic: Fuga said, “Because the government purchase price was high, the people’s price was low.

sentences.zh: 臣見司農識大體，不見其罪。」

translations.literal: I see that the Court of Imperial Granaries understood the larger principle; I do not see its crime.”
translations.idiomatic: I see that the Court of Imperial Granaries understood the larger principle; I do not see its crime.”

sentences.zh: 帝悟，顧悰曰：「卿不逮伏伽遠矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor understood, turned to Cong, and said, “You fall far short of Fuga.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood, turned to Cong, and said, “You fall far short of Fuga.”

sentences.zh: 久之，出為陝州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long while, Fuga was sent out as prefect of Shaanzhou and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, Fuga was sent out as prefect of Shaanzhou and then retired.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in Xianqing 3.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianqing 3.

sentences.zh: 始，伏伽拜御史時，先被內旨，而制未出，歸臥於家，無喜色。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Fuga was appointed censor, he first received a private edict while the formal appointment had not yet been issued. He returned and lay at home without a look of joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuga was first appointed censor, he received a private edict before the formal appointment was issued. He went home and lay down without a trace of joy on his face.

sentences.zh: 頃之，御史造門，子弟驚白，伏伽徐起見之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the censor came to his gate; his sons and younger brothers startled him with the news, and Fuga rose slowly to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an envoy from the censorate arrived at his door. His sons rushed to tell him, but Fuga rose slowly to receive the messenger.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其有量，以比顧雍雲。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised his magnanimity and compared him to Gu Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his composure and compared him to Gu Yong of old.

sentences.zh: 張玄素

translations.literal: Zhang Xuansu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuansu

sentences.zh: 張玄素，蒲州虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuansu was a man of Yuxiang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuansu was a native of Yuxiang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，為景城縣戶曹。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Household Officer of Jingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as household officer of Jingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 竇建德陷景城，執將殺之，邑人千餘號泣請代，曰：「此清吏，殺之是無天也。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande took Jingcheng, he seized Xuansu and was about to kill him. More than a thousand people of the district wept and begged to die in his place, saying, "This is an upright official—to kill him is to be without Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande captured Jingcheng, he seized Xuansu for execution. More than a thousand townspeople wept and begged to die in his place, crying, "He is an honest official—kill him and you defy Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 大王即定天下，無使善人解體。」

translations.literal: Great King, you are about to settle the realm—do not let good men lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Great King, you are about to settle the realm—do not dishearten good men.
