sentences.zh: 建德命釋縛，署治書侍御史，不拜。

translations.literal: Jiande ordered his bonds loosed and appointed him Attending Imperial Censor, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande ordered him released and appointed him attending imperial censor, but Xuansu refused the post.

sentences.zh: 聞江都已弑，始為建德黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When he heard that Jiangdu had been assassinated, he at last became Jiande's Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Only after learning that Jiangdu had fallen and the emperor murdered did he accept the post of vice director of the yellow gate under Jiande.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授景州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Army Adjutant for Records of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated he was appointed records adjutant in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，問以政，對曰：「自古未有如隋亂者，得非君自專、法日亂乎？

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he asked him about government. Xuansu answered, "From antiquity there has never been disorder like the Sui's—could it not be that the ruler acted on his own and the law grew daily more chaotic?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he asked Xuansu about government. Xuansu replied, "Never in history was there chaos like the Sui's. Was it not because the ruler acted alone while law fell daily into disorder?

sentences.zh: 且萬乘之尊，身決庶務，日斷十事，五不中，中者信善，有如不中者何？

translations.literal: Moreover, for the honor of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler to decide common affairs in person—if he decides ten matters a day and five are wrong, of the five that are right one may trust they are good; but what of those that are not right?
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven decides common affairs himself, deciding ten cases a day with five wrong—of the five right, one may trust they are sound; but what of the five wrong?

sentences.zh: 一日萬機，積其失，不亡何待？

translations.literal: In a single day ten thousand affairs—accumulate the errors, and what awaits if not ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand affairs in a day—accumulate such errors, and how can the state avoid ruin?

sentences.zh: 若上賢右能，使百司善職，則高居深拱，疇敢犯之？

translations.literal: If above one honors the worthy and to the right empowers the able, and makes the hundred offices perform their duties well, then seated high with hands folded deep in the sleeves—who would dare offend?
translations.idiomatic: If you honor the worthy above and empower the able, and let every office perform its duty, then seated high with folded hands—who would dare offend you?

sentences.zh: 隋末盜起，爭天下者不十數，餘皆保城邑以須有道聽命，是欲背上怙亂者果鮮，特人君不能安之而挻之亂也。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui bandits arose; those contending for the realm were not a dozen, while the rest all held city and town waiting for one who held the Way to receive their obedience. Those who truly wished to turn their backs on the ruler and cling to disorder were indeed few—it was only that the ruler could not settle them and instead pulled them into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, rebels rose everywhere, yet those truly fighting for empire were fewer than a dozen; the rest held their cities awaiting a ruler who held the Way. Few truly wished to rebel—the trouble was that rulers could not reassure them and instead drove them to revolt.

sentences.zh: 以陛下聖神，跡所以危，鑒所以亡，日慎一日，雖堯、舜何以加！」

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely spirit, tracing what brought danger and taking as mirror what brought ruin, being cautious day by day—even Yao and Shun could add nothing!
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagely spirit, tracing what brought danger and taking ruin as your mirror, growing more cautious day by day—even Yao and Shun could do no more!

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 拜侍御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor and transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attending censor, then promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，詔發卒治洛陽宮乾陽殿，且東幸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, an edict ordered conscripts to repair the Qianyang Hall of the Luoyang palace and also to travel east on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan an edict ordered laborers to repair the Qianyang Hall in the Luoyang palace and planned an eastern tour of the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄素上書曰：

translations.literal: Xuansu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣惟秦始皇帝藉周之餘，夷六國，統壹尊，將貽之萬世，及子而亡者，殫嗜奔欲，以逆天害人也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the First Emperor of Qin, relying on what remained of Zhou, overthrew the six states and unified them under one honor, intending to bequeath it for ten thousand generations—yet it perished with his son because he exhausted his desires in reckless pursuit and thereby opposed Heaven and harmed men.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the First Emperor of Qin, building on what remained of Zhou, conquered the six states and unified the realm for ten thousand generations—yet his line ended with his son because he exhausted every desire in reckless pursuit, opposing Heaven and harming the people.

sentences.zh: 天下不可以力勝，唯當務儉約，薄賦斂，以身先之，乃能大安。

translations.literal: The realm cannot be overcome by force alone; one must devote oneself to frugality, lighten levies and collections, and take the lead in person—only then can there be great peace.
translations.idiomatic: The realm cannot be secured by force alone. Only through frugality, light taxes, and leading by example can there be lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 今東都未有幸期，前事土木，戚王出籓，又當營構，科調繁仍，失疲人望，一不可也。

translations.literal: Now the eastern capital has no date for an imperial visit; earlier there was earth and timber work; the Prince of Qi has gone out to his fief and must again have construction—assessments and requisitions come in thick succession, losing the hope of the weary people. First, this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital has no fixed date for an imperial visit; construction has only just ended; the Prince of Qi has gone to his fief and needs new building—levies come one after another, betraying the hopes of an exhausted people. First, this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下向平東都，曾觀廣殿，皆撤毀之，天下翕然，一口頌歌。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty had just pacified the eastern capital, you once viewed the broad halls and had them all torn down; the realm was of one accord, with one mouth singing praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first pacified the eastern capital, you viewed the vast halls and had them torn down; the realm united as one in praise.

sentences.zh: 豈有初惡侈靡而後好雕麗哉？

translations.literal: How could one at first hate extravagance and afterward love carved splendor?
translations.idiomatic: Can you have hated extravagance at first and now love carved splendor?

sentences.zh: 二不可也。

translations.literal: Second, this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Second, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下每言巡幸者不急之務，徒焉虛費。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has often said that touring on campaign is not urgent business and is mere empty waste.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has often said that imperial tours are not urgent business and waste resources in vain.

sentences.zh: 今國儲無兼年，又興別都之役，以產怨讟，三不可也。

translations.literal: Now the state's stores do not last two years, yet another capital's labor is raised, producing resentment and slander. Third, this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: National stores will not last two years, yet you would raise labor for a second capital, breeding resentment. Third, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 百姓承亂離之後，財賦殫空，雖蒙更生，意未完定，奈何營未幸之都，重耗其力，四不可也。

translations.literal: The common people, after disorder and separation, have had wealth and levies utterly emptied; though they have received renewed life, their minds are not yet settled—how can you build an as-yet-unvisited capital and again exhaust their strength? Fourth, this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The people, after chaos and separation, are drained of wealth; though they have begun to recover, their minds are not yet settled—why build a capital you have not yet visited and exhaust them again? Fourth, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 漢祖將都洛陽，婁敬一言，即日西駕。

translations.literal: Han Founder was about to make Luoyang his capital; one word from Lou Jing, and that very day he turned his carriage west.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder was about to make Luoyang his capital, a single word from Lou Jing sent him west that very day.

sentences.zh: 非不知地土中，道裏所均，但形勝不及關內，弗敢康也。

translations.literal: It was not that he did not know the land was central and the roads equally balanced, but that its strategic advantage did not match Guanzhong—he did not dare be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that he did not know Luoyang stood at the center with roads equally balanced, but that its strategic strength could not match Guanzhong—he dared not rest easy there.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下化凋弊之俗，為日尚淺，詎可東巡以搖人心？

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's transforming of declining custom has not many days yet—how can you tour east and shake the people's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only begun to transform a broken society—how can you tour east and unsettle the people's hearts? Fifth, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 五不可也。

translations.literal: Fifth, this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗見隋家造殿，伐木于豫章，二千人挽一材，以鐵為轂，行不數里，轂輒壞，別數百人齎轂自隨，終日行不三十里。

translations.literal: Your servant once saw the Sui build a hall, felling timber in Yuzhang; two thousand men hauled one beam, with iron for the wheel hub; after going not several li the hub would break, and several hundred men separately carried hubs along—in a whole day they advanced not thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: I once saw the Sui build a hall, felling timber in Yuzhang. Two thousand men hauled a single beam on iron wheel hubs; after a few li the hubs broke, and hundreds more had to carry spare hubs—advancing barely thirty li in a whole day.

sentences.zh: 一材之費，已數十萬工，揆其餘可知已。

translations.literal: The cost of one beam was already several hundred thousand work-days; measuring the rest, one may know it.
translations.idiomatic: A single beam cost hundreds of thousands of work-days; the rest may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 昔阿房成，秦人散；

translations.literal: Formerly when Epang was completed, the Qin people scattered;
translations.idiomatic: When Epang was completed, the Qin people scattered;

sentences.zh: 章華就，楚眾離；

translations.literal: when Zhanghua was finished, the Chu masses departed;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhanghua was finished, the Chu people dispersed;

sentences.zh: 乾陽畢功，隋人解體。

translations.literal: when Qianyang was completed, the Sui people fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: when Qianyang was completed, the Sui fell apart.

sentences.zh: 今民力未及隋日，而役殘創之人，襲亡國弊，臣恐陛下之過，甚於煬帝。

translations.literal: Now the people's strength has not reached the Sui day, yet you employ men wounded and maimed, inheriting the ills of a perished state—I fear Your Majesty's fault exceeds Emperor Yang's.
translations.idiomatic: The people's strength has not recovered to Sui levels, yet you would employ the wounded and broken and repeat the errors of a fallen dynasty—I fear Your Majesty's fault may exceed even Emperor Yang's.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿謂我不如煬帝，何如桀、紂？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You say I am not equal to Emperor Yang—how about Jie and Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You say I am no better than Emperor Yang—am I then like Jie and Zhou of old?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若此殿卒興，同歸於亂。

translations.literal: He answered, "If this hall is completed and raised, we will end in the same disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If this hall is built to completion, the end will be the same—chaos.

sentences.zh: 臣聞東都始平，太上皇詔宮室過度者焚之，陛下謂瓦木可用，請賜貧人，事雖不從，天下稱為盛德，今復度而宮之，是隋役又興。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the eastern capital was first pacified, the Supreme Emperor ordered that excessive palaces be burned. Your Majesty said the tiles and timber could be used and asked to grant them to the poor. Though the matter was not followed, the realm called it great virtue. Now you again measure and make it a palace—this is the Sui labor raised anew.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital was first pacified, the retired emperor ordered excessive palaces burned. Your Majesty wished to give the timber to the poor. Though the plan was not carried out, the realm praised your virtue. Now you would measure and build again—Sui-style forced labor revived.

sentences.zh: 不五六年間，一舍一取，天下謂何？」

translations.literal: Within not five or six years, once abandoning and once taking back—what will the realm say?"
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years, first abandoning and then reclaiming—what will the realm think?"

sentences.zh: 帝顧房玄齡曰：「洛陽朝貢天下中，朕營之，意欲便四方百姓。

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to Fang Xuanling and said, "Luoyang receives tribute at the center of the realm. I build it intending to benefit the common people of the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Fang Xuanling and said, "Luoyang stands at the center of tribute from the realm. I build it to benefit the people of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 今玄素言如此，使後必往，雖露坐，庸何苦？」

translations.literal: Now Xuansu speaks thus; if later I must go, even sitting in the open air—what hardship would there be?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Xuansu speaks so forcefully, if I must go later, I would sit in the open air rather than cause such hardship."

sentences.zh: 即詔罷役，賜彩二百匹。

translations.literal: He immediately issued an edict to halt the labor and granted two hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He at once halted the project and granted Xuansu two hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 魏征名梗挺，聞玄秦言，歎曰：「張公論事，有回天之力，可謂仁人之言哉。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng was known for his upright stubbornness; hearing Xuansu's words, he sighed and said, "Master Zhang's discussion of affairs has the power to turn back Heaven—it may be called the words of a benevolent man.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng, known for his stubborn integrity, heard Xuansu's words and sighed, "Master Zhang's counsel has the power to turn back Heaven—truly the words of a benevolent man.

sentences.zh: 曆太子少詹事，遷右庶子。

translations.literal: He served successively as Junior Grand Mentor of the Heir and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior grand mentor of the heir, then was made right vice director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 時太子承乾事遊畋，不悅學。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Chenggan devoted himself to roaming and hunting and took no pleasure in study.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir Chenggan devoted himself to hunting and took no pleasure in study.

sentences.zh: 玄素上書曰：

translations.literal: Xuansu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 天道無親，惟德是輔。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way has no favorites; only virtue is assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way shows no partiality; it assists only virtue.

sentences.zh: 苟違天道，人神棄之。

translations.literal: If one violates Heaven's Way, men and spirits abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever violates Heaven's Way is abandoned by men and spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 古者田三驅，非以教殺，除民害也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the hunt drove on three sides—not to teach killing, but to remove harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the royal hunt drove game on three sides—not to teach killing, but to rid the people of pests.

sentences.zh: 今反以獵為娛，行之無常，不損盛德哉？

translations.literal: Now you instead take the hunt as amusement, practicing it without constant rule—does this not diminish great virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Now you take the hunt for amusement, practicing it without restraint—does this not diminish your great virtue?

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「事不師古，匪說攸聞。」

translations.literal: The Tradition says, "Matters that do not take antiquity as teacher—such talk is not heard.
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says, "Matters that do not follow antiquity—such counsel is never heard.

sentences.zh: 然則探道在學古，學古在師訓。

translations.literal: Thus probing the Way lies in studying antiquity, and studying antiquity lies in taking instruction as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: To seek the Way one must study antiquity; to study antiquity one must heed instruction.

sentences.zh: 孔潁達奉詔講勸，宜數逮問，裨萬分。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda, receiving the edict, lectures and encourages—you should frequently summon and question him, to assist you ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda lectures at imperial command—you should summon him often for instruction; it would benefit you beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 博選賢傑，朝夕侍左右，與相規摩。

translations.literal: Broadly select worthy heroes to attend at your left and right morning and evening, and with them mutually regulate and polish.
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy men broadly to attend you morning and evening and polish one another in counsel.

sentences.zh: 日知所亡，月無忘所能，此則善美矣。

translations.literal: Daily know what you lack; monthly forget not what you can do—this is goodness and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Know daily what you lack; forget not monthly what you have mastered—this is true excellence.

sentences.zh: 夫在人上者常求為善也，然性不勝情，耽惑成亂，下有諛言，君道乃虧。

translations.literal: Those above others constantly seek to do good, yet nature does not overcome emotion; indulgence and bewitchment become disorder; below there is flattery—the ruler's Way is thereby diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers constantly seek to do good, yet passion overcomes nature, indulgence breeds disorder, and flattery below undermines the ruler's Way.

sentences.zh: 古人有云：「勿以惡小不去，善小不為。」

translations.literal: The ancients said, "Do not let a small evil go because it is small; do not fail to do a small good because it is small.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Do not neglect a small evil because it is small; do not neglect a small good because it is small.

sentences.zh: 禍福之來，皆根于初，護終若始，猶懼其替，始不護焉，終將安歸？

translations.literal: Fortune and misfortune all take root at the beginning. To guard the end as the beginning—one still fears its decline. If at the beginning one does not guard, where will the end go?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune take root at the beginning. Guard the end as you did the beginning, yet still fear decline. Fail to guard at the start—where can the end lead?"

sentences.zh: 太子不納。

translations.literal: The Heir did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The heir would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又上書曰：

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 周公資聖人，而握沐吐飧，下白屋，況下周公之人哉？

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou had the endowment of a sage, yet he held the comb in the bath and spat out his food, went down to humble cottages—how much more should one below the Duke of Zhou do so?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou was endowed with sagehood, yet he attended others in the bath and shared his meal with humble scholars from thatched cottages—how much more should you, who stand below the Duke of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 殿下睿質天就，尚須學以表飾之。

translations.literal: Your Highness's keen substance is Heaven-given, yet you still need study to display and adorn it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's keen nature is Heaven-given, yet you still need learning to display and refine it.

sentences.zh: 孔穎達、趙弘智皆宿德钜髦，兼識政機，望數召見，述古今，增懿明德。

translations.literal: Kong Yingda and Zhao Hongzhi are both elders of long virtue and great leaders, and also understand the mechanisms of government. I hope you will frequently summon and see them, narrating past and present to increase your excellent bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda and Zhao Hongzhi are eminent elders who also understand statecraft. I urge you to summon them often to discourse on past and present and increase your bright virtue.

sentences.zh: 雕蟲小技，正可間召，代博弈，不宜屢也。

translations.literal: The petty skill of carved insects may rightly be summoned at intervals to replace gambling—it should not be frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Petty literary arts may be summoned occasionally to replace gambling, but not frequently.

sentences.zh: 騎射畋遊，褻戲酣歌，悅耳目，移情靈，不可以禦。

translations.literal: Riding, archery, hunting, roaming, licentious play, drunken song—pleasing the ears and eyes, shifting the spirit—cannot be defended against.
translations.idiomatic: Riding, archery, hunting, licentious games, and drunken song please the senses and shift the spirit—they cannot be resisted once indulged.

sentences.zh: 夫心為萬事主，動而無節則亂，敗德之原，實在於此。

translations.literal: The heart is master of the ten thousand affairs; moved without measure it becomes disorder. The source of ruined virtue lies truly here.
translations.idiomatic: The heart rules all affairs; moved without restraint it falls into disorder. The root of ruined virtue lies here.

sentences.zh: 帝知數財正太子，頻擢至銀青光祿大夫，行左庶子。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he repeatedly remonstrated to correct the Heir and frequently promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal, acting as Left Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he repeatedly admonished the heir and promoted him repeatedly to grand master of splendid happiness with the silver seal, acting as left vice director of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 太子久不見賓友，玄素曰：「宮中所見止婦人，不知如樊姬等可與益聖德者幾何？

translations.literal: The Heir had long not seen guests and friends. Xuansu said, "In the palace you see only women—I do not know how many like Fan Ji could increase sagely virtue?
translations.idiomatic: The heir had long avoided his advisers. Xuansu said, "In the palace you see only women. How many like Fan Ji are there who could increase your sagely virtue?

sentences.zh: 若無之，即便詖豔嬖，何足顧哉！

translations.literal: If there are none, then even slandering the beautiful favorites—what is there to care for!
translations.idiomatic: If there are none, why trouble yourself even to criticize your favorites?

sentences.zh: 上惟東宮之重，高署賢才為寮佐，今乃不得進見，將何以朝納誨、夕補遺哉？

translations.literal: Above, considering the weight of the Eastern Palace, high offices appoint worthy talent as assistants—yet now they cannot gain audience. How will you receive instruction in the morning and supply omissions in the evening?
translations.idiomatic: The throne values the eastern palace highly and appoints worthy men as your staff—yet they cannot gain audience. How will you receive morning instruction and evening correction?

sentences.zh: 太子諱其切，夜遣戶奴以騎楇狙擊，危脫死。

translations.literal: The Heir resented his sharpness; at night he sent a household slave with a mounted lance to ambush and strike him—he narrowly escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The heir resented his bluntness and sent a household slave by night with a mounted lance to ambush him; Xuansu narrowly escaped death.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞宮中擊鼓，叩閤正言，太子出鼓，對玄素破之。

translations.literal: Once he heard drums struck in the palace; knocking at the gate he spoke straight words. The Heir came out with the drum and broke it before Xuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Once he heard drums in the palace, knocked at the gate, and spoke plainly. The heir came out with the drum and smashed it before Xuansu's eyes.

sentences.zh: 既不悛，醜德日聞。

translations.literal: Since he would not reform, ugly conduct was daily heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since he would not reform, his misconduct grew daily more notorious.

sentences.zh: 玄素不能已，上書曰：

translations.literal: Xuansu could not stop himself and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold his tongue, Xuansu submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「能近取譬，可謂仁之方也。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Able to take what is near as comparison may be called the method of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "To find comparisons in what is near at hand is the method of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 書傳所載或過，臣請以近事喻之。

translations.literal: What books and traditions record may be remote; your servant asks to use recent affairs as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: What books record may seem remote; I ask to use recent events as comparison.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平山東，庳宮陋食以安海內，而太子贇有穢德，烏丸軌以聞，帝慈仁不忍廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified east of the mountains, with low palaces and plain food to settle the realm within the seas, yet the Heir Yun had foul conduct. Wuyuan Gui reported it; the Emperor was kindly and benevolent and could not bear to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified the east with humble palaces and plain food, yet his heir Yun behaved foully. Wuyuan Gui reported it, but the emperor's kindness kept him from deposition.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，狂暴日熾，宗祀以亡，隋文帝所代是也。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, violence and frenzy grew daily; the ancestral sacrifices perished thereby—this is what Emperor Wen of Sui replaced.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun took the throne, his violence grew daily until the dynasty fell—this is the house that Emperor Wen of Sui replaced.

sentences.zh: 文帝因周衰，藉女資，雖無大功於人，然布德行惠，上下安賴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, taking advantage of Zhou's decline and relying on a woman's resources, though without great merit toward others, yet spread virtue and practiced kindness; above and below relied on him in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen rose as Zhou declined, relying on his wife's connections. Though he won no great merit, he spread virtue and kindness, and above and below relied on him.

sentences.zh: 勇為太子，驕肆敗度，今宮中山池，殿下所親見者也。

translations.literal: Yong was Heir, arrogant and unrestrained beyond measure; the hills and pools in the palace today are what Your Highness has seen with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Yong was arrogant beyond all measure—the hills and pools in the palace today are what Your Highness has seen with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 當是時，自謂有太山之安，詎知壬臣敢進其說哉？

translations.literal: At that time he thought himself secure as Mount Tai—how could he know that a crafty minister would dare advance his schemes?
translations.idiomatic: At the time he thought himself secure as Mount Tai—how could he know a crafty minister would dare advance his schemes?

sentences.zh: 向使動靜有常，進止有度，親君子，疏小人，黜浮華，守恭儉，雖有離間，烏能致慈父之隙哉？

translations.literal: If only his movements and stillness had had constant rule, his advance and halt measured degree, drawing near to gentlemen and keeping petty men at a distance, dismissing floating show and keeping respectful frugality—even with alienation, how could he have brought a gap between a loving father and son?
translations.idiomatic: Had he kept regular conduct, measured his steps, drawn near to gentlemen and kept petty men away, dismissed extravagance and kept to respectful frugality—even with slander, how could a loving father's bond have been broken?

sentences.zh: 蓋積德弗純，令問不著，一遭讒，遂成其禍。

translations.literal: It was because accumulated virtue was not pure and fair reputation was not established—once slander struck, his disaster was thereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: But his virtue was impure and his reputation unsettled—one slander, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 今上以殿下父子親，故所資用不為限節，然詔未六旬，而用逾七萬，驕奢亡藝，孰有過此？

translations.literal: Now above, because Your Highness and father and son are close, what is supplied is not limited—but in not sixty days of edict, expenditure exceeds seventy thousand. Arrogant extravagance without limit—who exceeds this?
translations.idiomatic: Because father and son are close, Your Highness's expenses are not limited—yet in less than sixty days you have spent more than seventy thousand. Such arrogant extravagance—who has exceeded it?

sentences.zh: 龍樓、望苑，為工匠之肆，既闕視膳問安之宜，又無悅學好道之實。

translations.literal: The Dragon Tower and Prospect Garden have become workshops for craftsmen—already lacking the propriety of viewing meals and inquiring after health, and also without the reality of delighting in study and loving the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Tower and Prospect Garden have become workshops—neglecting the duty to inquire after your father's health, and showing no delight in learning or love of the Way.

sentences.zh: 上違君父慈訓之方，下有因緣戮辱之罪。

translations.literal: Above you violate the method of a father's kind instruction; below you have the crime of causing insult and shame by circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Above you violate a father's kind instruction; below you invite the shame of violence against your teachers.

sentences.zh: 所施與者，不遊手雜色，則圖畫雕鏤之人。

translations.literal: Those you bestow gifts on are none but idle hands and miscellaneous performers, or men of painting, carving, and inlay.
translations.idiomatic: Those you reward are none but idle performers or painters and craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 外所瞻仰，此失已暴，內隱密者，尚可勝計哉？

translations.literal: What those outside look up to—this fault is already exposed; what is hidden within—can it still be counted?
translations.idiomatic: What outsiders see is already scandal enough—what is hidden within, can it even be counted?

sentences.zh: 右庶子趙弘智經明行脩，臣謂宜數進召，以廣徽美；

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhao Hongzhi is clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct; your servant thinks he should frequently be summoned to advance and increase excellent beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Zhao Hongzhi is learned and upright; I believe you should summon him often to broaden your excellence;

sentences.zh: 今反猜嫌，謂妄相推引。

translations.literal: yet now you instead suspect and resent, saying he falsely recommends one another.
translations.idiomatic: yet now you suspect him and call it false mutual promotion."

sentences.zh: 從善若流，尚恐不逮，飾非拒諫，禍可既乎？

translations.literal: Following goodness like a flowing stream, one still fears not reaching it; adorning faults and rejecting remonstrance—can disaster be ended?
translations.idiomatic: To follow good counsel like a flowing stream and still fear falling short is wise—but to gloss over faults and reject remonstrance, can disaster be avoided?"

sentences.zh: 書入，太子怒，遣刺客伺之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Heir was angry and sent assassins to watch for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the heir flew into a rage and sent assassins to lie in wait for him.

sentences.zh: 會宮廢，玄素坐除名為民。

translations.literal: When the palace was abolished, Xuansu was punished by removal of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern palace was abolished, Xuansu was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召授潮州刺史，徙鄧州，訖不復親近。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned and appointed Governor of Chaozhou, transferred to Dengzhou, and to the end was never again brought near.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled and appointed governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to Dengzhou, and never again allowed near the heir.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，以老致仕。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong reign he retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 麟德初卒。

translations.literal: Early in Linde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Linde era.

sentences.zh: 始，玄素與孫伏伽在隋皆為令史，太宗嘗問玄素宦立所來，深自羞汗。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Xuansu and Sun Fuga under the Sui were both clerks. Taizong once asked Xuansu where his official standing came from, and he was deeply ashamed and sweating.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xuansu and Sun Fuga had both been clerks under the Sui. Taizong once asked Xuansu where his official career had begun, and Xuansu flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良見帝曰：「君子不失言于人，明主不失言於戲。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang saw the Emperor and said, "A gentleman does not lose words toward others; a clear-sighted ruler does not lose words in jest.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang said to the emperor, "A gentleman does not speak carelessly to others; a wise ruler does not speak carelessly even in jest.

sentences.zh: 故言則史書之，禮成之，樂歌之。

translations.literal: Therefore when words are spoken, the historians record them, ritual completes them, and music sings them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore speech is recorded by historians, completed by ritual, and sung in music.

sentences.zh: 居上能禮其臣，乃盡力以奉其上。

translations.literal: When one above can treat his ministers with ritual, they then exhaust their strength to serve him above.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler treats his ministers with respect, they exhaust themselves in his service.

sentences.zh: 近世宋武帝侮靳朝臣，攻其門戶，至恥懼狼狽，前史以為非。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Wu of Song insulted and stinted court ministers, attacked their factions, until they were shamed, fearful, and in disarray—former histories judged this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Wu of Song insulted and stinted his ministers and attacked their factions until they were shamed and fearful—histories judge this wrong.

sentences.zh: 陛下昨問玄素在隋任何官，對曰：'縣尉。

translations.literal: Yesterday Your Majesty asked what office Xuansu held under the Sui; he answered, 'County Commandant.'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Your Majesty asked what office Xuansu held under the Sui. He answered, 'County commandant.'

sentences.zh: '又問未為尉時，曰：'流外。

translations.literal: You again asked before he was commandant; he said, 'Outside the regular stream.'
translations.idiomatic: You asked what he was before that. He said, 'Outside the regular stream.'

sentences.zh: '又問何曹司，玄素出不能徙步，顏若此灰，精爽頓盡，見者鹹共驚怪。

translations.literal: You again asked which bureau and office; Xuansu went out unable to move his steps, his face like ashes, his spirit suddenly exhausted—all who saw were together startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: You asked which bureau he served in. Xuansu left unable to walk, his face ashen, his spirit broken—all who saw were astonished.

sentences.zh: 唐家創業，任官以才，卜祝庸保，量能並用。

translations.literal: When the house of Tang founded its enterprise, it appointed officials by talent; diviners, prayers, menials, and guards—all were employed according to measured capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang founded its enterprise, it appointed by talent—diviners, attendants, and guards alike were used according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 陛下以玄素擢任三品，佐皇儲，豈宜復對群臣使辭窮負恥，欲責其伏節死義，安可得乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty promoted Xuansu to third rank to assist the imperial heir—how could you again before the host of ministers make his words exhausted and burden him with shame, wishing to charge him with holding to integrity and dying for righteousness—how could it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty promoted Xuansu to third rank to assist the heir—how can you shame him before the whole court and then expect him to die for righteousness?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕亦悔之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "We too regret it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I regret it as well."

sentences.zh: 伏伽雖廣坐，陳說往事，無少隱焉。

translations.literal: Fuga, though in a broad assembly, narrated past affairs without the least concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Fuga, though in open assembly, spoke of past affairs without the least concealment.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：始唐有天下，懲刈隋敝，敷內讜言，而世長等仇然獻忠，時主方褒聽，藉以勸天下，雖觸禁忌，而無忤情。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: When Tang first had the realm, it punished and cut away Sui's ills and spread forth remonstrance within. Men like Shichang and the rest, with stern countenance, offered loyalty; the ruler of the time was just praising and listening, using this to encourage the realm. Though they touched taboos, there was no offense to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: When the Tang first won the realm, it corrected the ills of the Sui and encouraged frank counsel within the court. Men like Shichang offered loyal remonstrance with stern faces while the ruler praised and heeded them, using their example to encourage the realm. Though they touched taboos, they gave no offense.

sentences.zh: 及禍亂已平，君位尊安，後者視前人之為，猶以鯁論期榮，故時時遭斥讓，為所厭苦。

translations.literal: When disaster and disorder were already pacified and the ruler's position was honored and secure, those who came after viewed the conduct of those before as still expecting glory through blunt argument, and therefore were repeatedly rebuked and reproached, becoming what was detested and suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Once chaos was pacified and the throne secure, later remonstrators still expected glory through blunt speech and were repeatedly rebuked and resented.

sentences.zh: 非言有巧拙，所遭之時異也。

translations.literal: It was not that the words had skill or clumsiness—the times encountered were different.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that their words were clever or clumsy—the times had changed.

sentences.zh: 夫性有不可移，雖堯、舜弗能訓。

translations.literal: Some natures cannot be moved—even Yao and Shun could not instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Some natures cannot be moved—even Yao and Shun could not reform them.

sentences.zh: 承乾之惡，根著於心，而歸責玄素，其何救哉？

translations.literal: Chenggan's wickedness was rooted and fixed in the heart, yet blame was returned upon Xuansu—what salvation could there be?
translations.idiomatic: Chenggan's wickedness was rooted in his heart, yet blame fell on Xuansu—what could save him?

sentences.zh: 此士亹辭不能傅太子，諒矣。

translations.literal: That this scholar with earnest words could not instruct the Heir—this is understandable.
translations.idiomatic: That earnest words could not instruct the heir is no surprise.
